name: contrarian-composite-inversion
rationale: This is the decisive sign test on the whole TA composite, and shirube's own accumulated dose-response is what motivates it rather than any outside claim. Three independent measurements now line up on one axis. (a) AMPLIFYING the composite is severely harmful: ta-weight-085-signal-amplitude (rejected 2026-09-13) cost 14.034 of Sharpe absolute and added 7.82pp of drawdown. (b) DAMPING it helps monotonically: the zone-band family measured Sharpe improving at every reduced amplitude (x0.90 promoted as PR #27, x0.85 and x0.80 both improving; 2026-09-18 recorded x0.80 as the largest Sharpe gain this pipeline has ever produced, +6.247 absolute), and every one of those variants died on MIN_TRADE_COUNT_RATIO rather than on performance. (c) The neutral point is still not good enough: seven consecutive runs now show a negative sharpe_minus_static_mix, today's at -1.5346 on the primary capital and -26.67 at 500,000 JPY. A signal whose performance improves monotonically as its gain falls toward zero, and degrades sharply as its gain rises, is the signature of a NEGATIVE-edge signal, and the extrapolation of that line past gain 0 has never been tested. Today's diagnostic capitals make the negative edge unmistakable and unattributable to direction: BTC rose 10.22% over the window, yet the strategy returned -10.84% at 500,000 JPY and -7.33% at 5,000,000 JPY on 812 and 818 trades, at win rates of 0.1397 and 0.1386. Losing 86% of round trips in a rising market is not noise around zero edge; it is a systematically wrong-sided signal. Note that contrarian-trend-subsignals (rejected 2026-09-15) does NOT already answer this: it inverted only the three trend-family sub-signals, which at TREND_SUBSIGNAL_WEIGHT 0.25 against REVERSION_SUBSIGNAL_WEIGHT 1.0 carry just 0.75 of the 2.75 total weight, so it flipped roughly 27% of the composite and left the two dominant mean-reverting sub-signals pointing the same way as before. This hypothesis inverts the AGGREGATE, after the weighted mean, so it flips 100% of the TA contribution in one place. It is also expected to preserve turnover almost exactly, which matters because the trade-count floor has been the binding rejection criterion on essentially every recent verdict: mirroring the target about 0.5 mirrors every allocation delta without changing its magnitude, so the lot-size floor accepts and refuses the same set of intents. The honest caveat, which must be carried into any PR: a sign flip is the most overfit-prone change this pipeline can make, a 14-day holdout cannot establish that the sign is stable across regimes, and the expected arithmetic is modest even if the premise is right -- inverting a cost-dominated loser returns the gross edge with the sign reversed while still paying the same costs. A promotion here is a request for careful human scrutiny, not a recommendation to ship.
code_change_summary: In TradingEngine::compute_btc_target (src/trading/engine.rs), invert the AGGREGATED technical composite exactly once, immediately after the weighted mean that produces `ta_normalized` and before it is combined with sentiment. Concretely, where the function currently computes `let ta_normalized = sub_signals.iter().map(|(v, w)| v * w).sum::<f64>() / weight_sum;`, keep that line unchanged and follow it with a single inversion step, expressed through a named private helper so the diff reads as one decision -- e.g. `fn invert_composite(ta: f64) -> f64 { 1.0 - ta }` with a doc comment -- and use the inverted value in the `combined` expression. Change NOTHING else: not the individual sub-signal formulas, not damped_cross, not CROSS_SATURATION, not either family weight, not which family weight each sub-signal is pushed with, not the weighted-mean aggregation or its divisor, not the empty-sub_signals warmup guard that returns None, not the sentiment normalization or the ta_weight/sentiment_weight combination, and not the final clamp. Because the weighted mean is a convex combination of values already in [0.0, 1.0], ta_normalized is in [0.0, 1.0], so 1.0 - ta_normalized is too and the function's existing range guarantee is preserved by construction -- state that in a comment. Document the change with a NOTE comment naming this hypothesis and stating the mechanism under test (shirube's own measured gain/performance relationship is monotonically decreasing, so the extrapolated optimum gain is negative; this tests gain = -1 on the aggregate). Add unit tests in the same module: (a) a strongly bullish point (RSI 20, close well above both sma and ema, positive histogram, low %B) asserting the returned composite is now BELOW the neutral 0.5 midpoint where it was previously above it; (b) the mirror bearish case asserting the composite is now above 0.5; (c) a point whose sub-signals aggregate to exactly 0.5, asserting the result is unchanged, i.e. the inversion is neutral-preserving; (d) an all-None IndicatorPoint asserting the warmup guard still returns None and the inversion is never reached; (e) a point supplying only RSI, asserting the composite equals ta_weight * (1.0 - (1.0 - rsi/100)) + sentiment_weight * 0.5 for a concrete rsi value, pinning the inversion's placement AFTER aggregation rather than before it. Update any existing compute_btc_target_* unit test whose expected value legitimately changes under the inversion -- in particular compute_btc_target_neutral_rsi_returns_some should still read ~0.5 and is a useful check that it does -- and do not weaken or delete a test to make it pass. Additionally instrument and REPORT (via stderr logging or a scratch harness only -- do NOT add a field to BacktestReport) the realised min/max/mean of the post-inversion composite over the evaluated window, so the report can confirm the band is the mirror of the baseline's rather than a differently-shaped distribution.
constraints: This hypothesis DOES modify TradingEngine::compute_btc_target's body. That is permitted under experiments/hypotheses/README.md's '`compute_btc_target` may be modified' section, but ONLY on this hypothesis's own dedicated isolation: "worktree" branch, and it MUST be reported explicitly so the coordinator flags it in any PR description.
MUST NOT change compute_btc_target's SIGNATURE. Only its body may change.

MUST NOT change any individual sub-signal formula, damped_cross, CROSS_SATURATION, REVERSION_SUBSIGNAL_WEIGHT, TREND_SUBSIGNAL_WEIGHT, the family weight each sub-signal is pushed with, the weighted-mean aggregation or its divisor, the empty-sub_signals warmup guard returning None, the sentiment normalization, the ta_weight/sentiment_weight combination, or the final clamp. The ONLY change is one inversion of the aggregated TA composite.
MUST NOT touch apply_zone, sticky_target, block_start, allocation_delta_to_order, the lot-size check, the orders_below_min counting arm, the RiskManager call sequence, or the fee logic.

MUST pass `cargo test`, including every existing compute_btc_target_* unit test. Update an expected value only where the inversion legitimately changes it, and do not weaken or delete a test just to make it pass.

MUST NOT fit anything on the holdout window, or on any window at all. This change introduces no tunable constant -- the inversion is exact (1.0 - ta) and is not a parameter to be scaled. If a partial inversion looks better, that is a separate hypothesis to propose, not a value to tune mid-run.
MUST NOT change src/signal/engine.rs's broadcast cadence or anything about live scheduling.

A promoted change still becomes its own PR against dev (per the pipeline's step 6) and is never merged automatically -- a human reviews it like any other algorithm hypothesis. Flag explicitly in the PR description that this diff touches compute_btc_target's body, that it REVERSES the direction of the entire technical composite, and that it therefore changes the allocation target the live engine acts on in a way a reviewer must scrutinise before it reaches real money.
MUST NOT touch src/exchange/bitflyer/*, .github/workflows/*, or the order-submission mechanics themselves.
